chapter: Mamie Smith and the New York dance bands
title: Walter Johnson and the Friendly Fifty club
summary: Walter Johnson, a New York drummer, was at the dance school; Caldwell describes the Friendly Fifty club of veteran musicians.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Oh, I see. Walter Johnson, you said. Right?
Well, now where did you meet him?
Walter was working at the dance school when I left Mamie. Dornell and them (Unintelligible) -- Benny was playing C-melody, and I was playing alto, and Benny gave me his job, and Walter was on drum.
Walter was on drum, right. Yeah, he's a New York boy.
Yeah. Yeah, he -- have you seen him lately?

We belong to the same club. See, they got a club called the Friendly Fifty, where I -- where they decided, every time you don't see one of the old fellows, only at funeral all you have, somebodys (unintelligible). So we decided we going to make a club, no politics or anything, just for us to get together and see each other. Once each and every month they have regular meetings, and they have the outing in August. Then we have the regular November cocktail dinner and dance. Doc (unintelligible) comes there. Lot of them come from Europe, was over during that time. They're all invited. And we have a good time.
Well, is Walter still working down on Wall Street?
I think he ought to do one of these things because he must have a lot of stories about Fletch.

Oh, he can. Yes, he can, because -- who covered him? Somebody, I think Doc Varner taped him, and we had a thing up there in Doc Varner's place at Larchmont four Saturdays ago, and they had this group from Sweden. People wanted to call in some of the jazz men, responsible for a lot of jazz work, and we had a beautiful turnout. Everybody played, took pictures (unintelligible) and all.
